source_facts.fact: City Hall states the London Plan 2021 remains the current adopted planning framework while the replacement Draft London Plan is in consultation from July to October 2026, with examination in 2027 and adoption expected in early 2028.
source_facts.gate: Draft 2026 policies must not be treated as adopted current policy.

source_facts.fact: The July 2026 Draft London Plan includes MBUL5 Sustainable Transport to enable London's Growth and says it applies to all local plans and development.
source_facts.gate: The policy is consultation material and cannot override the adopted London Plan 2021 before adoption.

source_facts.fact: The adopted plan supports a strategic target for 80 percent of London trips to be by foot, cycle or public transport by 2041.
source_facts.gate: Strategic mode-share target is not measured parcel travel behaviour.

source_facts.fact: The adopted London Plan says transport networks will need to cater for over five million additional trips per day by 2041.
source_facts.gate: Citywide forecast must not be downscaled into parcel trip generation.

source_facts.fact: TfL defines PTAL using walk time to public transport and service wait time, while TIM reports travel-time catchments through the network.
source_facts.gate: PTAL/TIM are connectivity tools and not planning permission, legal access or guaranteed capacity.

source_facts.fact: TfL says strategic developments referable to the Mayor normally require a Transport Assessment unless another approach is agreed; limited-impact schemes may use a Transport Statement.
source_facts.gate: Assessment requirement does not itself determine permission outcome.

source_facts.fact: City Hall reports over 12,000 Santander Cycles around 800 docking stations, more than 17,000 TfL-funded cycle parking spaces since 2019 and over 40,000 additional spaces planned by 2030.
source_facts.gate: Network totals and planned provision are not proof of availability at a parcel.

source_facts.fact: NPPF paragraph 118 says developments generating significant movement should provide a travel plan and a vision-led transport statement or assessment.
source_facts.gate: National policy evidence must be applied proportionately and alongside the adopted development plan.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current versus draft London Plan status
official_measurement_examples.fact: City Hall says the London Plan 2021 remains current; the Draft London Plan consultation runs July–October 2026, examination is expected in 2027 and adoption in early 2028.

official_measurement_examples.name: Draft MBUL5 sustainable transport policy
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 Draft London Plan presents MBUL5 Sustainable Transport to enable London's Growth, applying to all local plans and development, but the page is explicitly draft consultation material.

official_measurement_examples.name: London Plan 2021 strategic transport target
official_measurement_examples.fact: Adopted London Plan Policy T1 supports a strategic target for 80% of all trips in London to be made by foot, cycle or public transport by 2041.

official_measurement_examples.name: London Plan 2041 additional trip context
official_measurement_examples.fact: The adopted London Plan states London's transport networks will need to cater for over five million additional trips every day by 2041.

official_measurement_examples.name: TfL WebCAT PTAL semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: TfL defines PTAL as connectivity to the public transport network combining walk time with service wait times, while TIM maps travel-time catchments through the network.

official_measurement_examples.name: TfL Transport Assessment scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: TfL says developments of strategic importance referable to the Mayor should normally prepare a Transport Assessment unless another approach is agreed in writing; limited-impact cases may use a Transport Statement.

official_measurement_examples.name: Cycling network and parking programme context
official_measurement_examples.fact: City Hall reports over 12,000 Santander Cycles at around 800 docking stations, more than 17,000 cycle parking spaces funded by TfL since 2019 and over 40,000 additional spaces planned by 2030.

official_measurement_examples.name: NPPF significant movement transport evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF paragraph 118 says developments generating significant movement should provide a travel plan and be supported by a vision-led transport statement or assessment.

core_rules: the current adopted London Plan 2021 must not be replaced by the July 2026 draft before adoption
a draft London Plan policy is consultation evidence and not an adopted development-plan policy
draft-plan consultation dates must be preserved and not represented as adoption dates
PTAL is a public-transport accessibility measure and not a planning permission
PTAL does not measure every walking, cycling, road, freight or private-vehicle condition
a high PTAL does not guarantee spare public-transport capacity for a development
a low PTAL does not automatically make development unacceptable
future PTAL depends on future network assumptions and must not be treated as delivered infrastructure
WebCAT travel-time catchments are modelled accessibility evidence and not guaranteed journey times
WebCAT statistics must not be converted into parcel land value or Future Growth scores
transport connectivity is not the same as legal access to a parcel
proximity to a station does not guarantee station capacity or step-free access
proximity to a bus stop does not guarantee service frequency, reliability or future routing
current service frequency must not be assumed unchanged over a development lifetime
planned transport intervention is not completed transport infrastructure
funding approval is not construction completion
construction completion is not proof of operational capacity for every future development
transport safeguarding is not development permission
transport safeguarding land can constrain development and must be checked against exact geometry
an Opportunity Area growth objective is not a parcel allocation or planning permission
the 80 percent sustainable-mode target for 2041 is a strategic target and not a parcel observation
mode-share targets must not be represented as measured site travel behaviour
Healthy Streets policy is a planning framework and not a measured street-quality score for a parcel
Healthy Streets indicators require site-specific assessment before use
Vision Zero ambition is not evidence that a road has zero collision risk
cycling network presence is not proof of route quality, continuity or safety for a specific journey
cycle parking policy standards are not evidence that existing cycle parking is available
planned cycle parking is not delivered cycle parking
Santander Cycles fleet totals are network-level context and not dock availability at a site
dock availability is time-varying and must not be inferred from total docking-station counts
electric-vehicle chargepoint counts are not proof of charger availability at a specific time
public chargepoint proximity is not proof of power capacity for a development
EV infrastructure strategy is not a site-specific connection approval
Approved Document S compliance is not planning permission
building-regulations EV requirements must not be confused with London Plan parking policy
EV business-rates relief is a fiscal measure and not evidence of charger delivery
Congestion Charge or ULEZ rules are road-user charging policy and not a development viability score
road-user charge boundaries must not be treated as cadastral parcel boundaries
Transport Assessment requirements are proportionate to development impacts and context
a Transport Assessment is not itself an approval or refusal
a Transport Statement is not interchangeable with a full Transport Assessment where impacts are significant
severe transport impact is a planning judgement and must not be inferred from a single metric
trip generation estimates are model outputs and not observed future trips
travel-plan targets are management commitments and not guaranteed behaviour outcomes
travel-plan monitoring must preserve baseline, period and responsibility
planning obligations must be necessary and justified; they are not automatic charges for every development
Section 106 transport contributions are not proof that a transport scheme is funded in full
CIL receipt is not proof of project allocation, delivery or completion
MCIL funding context is not parcel-specific transport mitigation evidence
freight and servicing plans are not proof of road capacity
construction logistics plans are temporary-management evidence and not permanent transport capacity
delivery and servicing requirements must remain distinct from passenger transport accessibility
parking maximums are policy standards and not observed parking demand
car-free policy starting points must be read with location, accessibility and disabled-parking requirements
Blue Badge parking requirements must not be removed by general car-free assumptions
future parking standards must not be backdated to already determined applications
road hierarchy or red-route status is not proof of unrestricted site access
highway licence requirements are not planning permission
working near TfL assets can require separate approvals that must not be inferred from planning consent
conveyancing search evidence is not a planning decision
transport modelling assumptions must preserve model year, scenario and network inputs
modelled congestion is not the same as observed congestion
historical congestion evidence must not be treated as a future guaranteed condition
active-travel infrastructure presence does not prove accessibility for every user
step-free accessibility must be checked independently from general PTAL or station proximity
accessibility improvements announced in strategy are not delivered until independently evidenced
public-transport capacity mitigation must be checked at the relevant line, station, stop or corridor
development-related transport mitigation is not a substitute for exact parcel planning-policy checks
national NPPF sustainable-transport policy must be read alongside the adopted development plan
local and national transport policies can overlap but must not be double-counted as independent evidence
duplicate official pages describing the same policy are one evidence family, not independent corroboration
source confidence is research-source confidence and not parcel-level transport accuracy
RECOVERY_PARKED forbids parcel relation creation, Future Growth scoring and business promotion
